name: Greater plantain (Plantago major)
short: Lab: water extracts were genotoxic in fruit flies (another test found no mutagenicity). Small trials, by mouth or on the skin, reported no significant side effects. Human safety data are limited.
text: Human safety data on greater plantain (not the psyllium species Plantago ovata) come from small, short trials. In a 10-day placebo-controlled trial of a syrup taken by mouth in 80 adults with acute bronchitis, no significant adverse effects were reported in either group, and in a trial of a topical formulation in 130 patients with stage 1 pressure ulcers, no side effects of the formulation were found. In a 12-week placebo-controlled trial in 72 obese women, oral Plantago major raised blood leptin levels, and the authors suggested that this may intensify endothelial dysfunction and angiogenesis; this is their interpretation of blood markers, not an observed clinical harm. In laboratory testing, aqueous extracts of Plantago major were genotoxic (recombinagenic) in a fruit-fly somatic cell test, whereas in another study hydroalcoholic extracts were not mutagenic with or without metabolic activation. The abstracts do not report on pregnancy or long-term use. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
